name: Lakeside Trading, Sheds & Outdoor Furniture
about:
Lakeside Trading LLC has operated from Narragansett, Rhode Island since 1999, when founder Dave Harrigan liquidated his 401(k) to purchase a trailer load of hand-made clay chimineas from Mexico. The family-owned business began as a wholesale and seasonal market venture before Harrigan encountered Pennsylvania shed builders during East Coast buying trips. Recognizing a gap in the Rhode Island market, he acquired a shed-moving trailer and leased a former 19th-century fishing equipment warehouse on South Pier Road, establishing a permanent location that he purchased outright in 2010.

Today the company maintains a 5,000-square-foot showroom and an expansive display yard staffed by 20 full-time employees, several with more than 15 years of tenure. Lakeside Trading does not manufacture its own products; instead it procures, installs, and services American-made sheds, greenhouses, chicken coops, gazebos, garages, pergolas, playsets, and pavilions, along with outdoor furniture crafted from recycled plastic poly lumber and marine-grade hardware. The team installs more than 1,000 structures and sells over 2,000 furniture pieces each year, and also provides site preparation such as gravel or stone pads, rock pads, and shed relocation services.

The primary customer base is residential homeowners throughout Rhode Island seeking durable outdoor storage and living solutions. Projects range from simple garden sheds and Adirondack chairs to custom-designed pavilions, greenhouses converted into art studios, and chicken coops with epoxy floors and automatic doors. The company also handles used-shed purchases, moving and reinstalling them on prepared foundations.

Lakeside Trading differentiates itself through Amish-crafted structures backed by a 10-year warranty and a lifetime service guarantee, free on-site consultations before purchase, and a commitment to fair pricing. The business remains locally owned and operated, emphasizing personal service from sales through installation.

name: Lance Industries
old_description: Since 1985, Lance Industries has manufactured high-quality commercial meat marinators and vacuum meat tumblers. You can find Lance Industries’ equipment across the globe in meat markets, grocery stores, butcher shops, delis, restaurants, and meat processing facilities.
about:
Lance Industries has been building vacuum meat tumblers in Hartford, Wisconsin since 1985. The company was founded to give U.S. meat processors a durable, reliable alternative to imported equipment, becoming the first American-made meat tumbler on the market. Its designs originated from collaboration with Family Farms Meats and the engineering staff at LMI Manufacturing.

The product line comprises four models ranging from 50 to 1,000 pounds of capacity: the LT-5, LT-15, LT-30, and LT-60. Each unit features variable-speed rotation, a digital timer, built-in vacuum, and wheels that allow it to pass through a standard 32-inch door. Drums are constructed from thicker-gauge steel with removable lids and metal-detectable gaskets for sanitation. More than 3,000 tumblers have been installed worldwide, and the company maintains a fully stocked service and repair department.

Customers include meat markets, grocery stores, butcher shops, delis, restaurants, meat processing facilities, and meat-alternative processors. Testimonials cite operations such as Haun's Meat & Sausage, Bardini's Country Smokehouse, Bob's Processing, Hudson Meats, and Quality Cut Meats. Lance also works with domestic and international dealers and participates in the American Association of Meat Processors and the Wisconsin Association of Meat Processors.

The company emphasizes mobility, durability, and U.S.-based technical support as key differentiators. Its tumblers are engineered to reduce marination and curing times, improve yield, and deliver consistent product quality batch after batch.

about:
Landmark Packaging Inc. was founded in 2012 in Aurora, Colorado, by Mark, Paul, and Jeff. The trio set out to establish a packaging supplier focused on small and medium-sized businesses in the Rocky Mountain region.

The company operates as both a manufacturer and distributor of packaging materials, offering stock and custom boxes, bags, labels, containers, janitorial supplies, and personal protective equipment. Its capabilities include digital printing on packaging, custom box fabrication, and fulfillment services such as labeling, poly bagging, stretch wrapping, shrink wrapping, taping, and bubble wrapping. The operation runs from a facility with more than 48,000 square feet of warehouse space.

Landmark Packaging primarily serves small and medium-sized businesses throughout Colorado, providing packaging solutions for a range of commercial and industrial customers.

The founders started the business to address a gap in affordable custom packaging for smaller companies, aiming to deliver quality materials and services at prices that fit tight budgets. The company emphasizes its focus on small and mid-sized clients as a core differentiator.

Lang's Old Car Parts, Inc. operates from Baldwinville, Massachusetts. The company remains under family stewardship, though specific founders are not named in public materials.

The company maintains what it describes as the most complete catalog of Model T Ford parts on the market, offering both new and used components as well as new-old-stock (NOS) items. Beyond parts, the inventory includes accessories, books, and instructional movies. Free technical support is provided by a staff in which three-quarters reportedly own a Model T themselves. Lang's serves Model T enthusiasts, hobbyists, and restorers — primarily individuals restoring or maintaining Ford Model T automobiles and Fordson tractors. The customer base spans antique automobile restoration and vintage automotive hobbyist sectors.

The business emphasizes its family-owned heritage and the personal passion of its staff as differentiators. It was started to fill a gap in the availability of correct, quality Model T parts and to offer the technical guidance that hobbyists often need.

about:
Largo Tank & Equipment Inc. operates from Farmington, New Mexico, where it has built custom truck and tank equipment for over 25 years. The company was established to serve the demanding off-road and heavy-duty needs of the Southwest, though its exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The facility designs, welds, and installs a range of built-to-order products including truck bodies (flatbeds, service bodies, crane bodies, contractor beds, van bodies), cargo tanks for propane, refined fuels, and chemical treaters, and fire equipment such as skid-mounted units and forestry bodies. It also maintains a large inventory of hard-to-find parts representing hundreds of brands and provides 24/7 repair service. All fabrication is performed at the Farmington shop.

The customer base spans oil and gas, propane distribution, construction, fuel delivery, mining, crane service, general delivery, fire and emergency services, government fleets, agriculture, plumbing, and landscaping. Typical projects include oilfield bodies for the San Juan Basin, municipal utility vehicles, and wildland fire response units.

Largo emphasizes close collaboration on custom design, aiming to make each project easier for the operator and to deliver equipment that withstands extreme off-road conditions. The company’s stated goal is to “build it right every time” through innovative engineering and responsive service.

name: Larson Cable Trailers, Inc
old_description: Founded in 2000 by Rick Larson, Larson Cable Trailers revolutionized the industry as the original creator of the patented cable fiber installation trailer.
about:
Larson Cable Trailers, Inc. was founded in 2000 by Rick Larson in Huron, South Dakota. The company originated from Larson's underground utilities business, Larson Digging Inc., where he needed a trailer that could lift cable reels, "figure 8," and rewind cable efficiently. Unable to find a suitable solution, he engineered his own patented cable fiber installation trailer. In 2024, the business was acquired by Felling Trailers and continues to operate as a separate division, leveraging the resources of a full-line trailer manufacturer with over 240 models.

The company manufactures patented reel-handling trailers designed for fiber-optic and power utility installations. Its core product line includes trailers that combine reel lifting, figure-8 cable layout, and rewinding in a single unit. Larson Cable Trailers also supplies replacement parts, manuals, and warranty services through an online parts store launched in 2024. Early that year, the division expanded its portfolio with the addition of the Drive Trailers product line, broadening its range of trailer solutions.

Customers include public and private contractors, rural telephone cooperatives, electric cooperatives, and city municipalities across the United States. The equipment is used by firms such as K&H Electric Inc. of Linton, North Dakota, which cited the trailer's versatility in eliminating the need for multiple separate machines.

Larson's founding premise was to solve a real-world problem: existing trailers could not perform the combined functions required for efficient cable installation. The company emphasizes patented designs that improve crew productivity, durability in harsh conditions, and reliability that helps crews lay more cable in less time. Its stated mission is to drive efficiency and innovation in cable installation by working directly with installation crews to refine equipment.

name: Latest Metalworks
old_description: ISO 9001-Certified Metal Fabrication with Over 20 Years of Large-Scale Program Experience
about:
Based in Murrieta, California, Latest Metalworks, Inc. was founded nearly two decades ago with a mission to bring clients' visions to life through custom metal fabrication. The company operates from Riverside County and serves customers nationally.

The shop provides full-program fabrication from engineering review through final delivery. Core processes include flat and tube laser cutting on an AMADA fiberoptic system, waterjet cutting on an OMAX machine, forming and bending on an Amada press brake, 8-axis tube bending and rolling, LADBS-certified welding, and in-house engineering using SolidWorks. Secondary finishing, fitment, assembly, and a dedicated packaging department support production runs, structural assemblies, exhibit structures, prototype programs, and architectural metalwork.

Latest Metalworks serves automotive OEM, industrial, architectural, EV and solar, and R&D sectors, with documented work for aerospace suppliers and municipal water departments. Clients include the Temeka Group for retail and museum projects, the City of Oceanside Water Department for plant maintenance, Inokinetic for aerospace components, and tooling firms such as Tube Bending Technology and V&T Tooling.

The company emphasizes combining traditional craftsmanship with current technology, citing its ISO 9001:2015 certification and LADBS structural steel fabricator approval as foundations for quality. A problem-solving, forward-thinking mindset and in-house equipment aim to reduce lead times and control quality from prototype to production.

old_description: Since 1983, Laurel Wire has worked with a wide array of industries and manufacturers to deliver quality parts on time to meet customer specs. Our humble beginnings as a small
about:
Laurel Wire Company, Inc. was founded in 1983 in Plainville, Connecticut, by Dick Clark and his business partner William Killiany. The two opened the business in Clark's garage on Laurel Street, driven by Clark's goal of a passionate commitment to the customer.

The company provides wire straightening, cutting, and centerless grinding services, along with Swiss screw machining. It processes round wire and strip material in diameters from 0.030 to 0.364 inches and lengths up to 40 feet, using a range of alloys and tempers. Centerless grinding is offered as through-feed service. The firm does not produce or warehouse raw material; it purchases material to customer specifications.

Laurel Wire serves manufacturers across industries including automotive, aerospace, industrial components, jewelry, fishing lures, springs, tubing mandrels, acoustical ceilings, pipe organs, bookbinding, extension drills, hinges, wire forms, heating elements, and wire warehousing. Its customer base ranges from prototyping to large-scale production.

The company emphasizes customizable solutions, constant communication, and fast, reliable service. It aims to minimize scrap loss and maximize precision, drawing on over 40 years of experience to meet exact specifications.
